summary.headline: Tatva Chintan Q4 FY26 operating revenue rose 24% YoY to INR1,341 million, with EBITDA of INR281 million (about 21% margin); FY27 guidance held at ~25% growth and 20-22% EBITDA margin.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 operating revenue was INR1,341 million, up 24% YoY and 2% QoQ, with EBITDA of INR281 million, up 214% YoY and 10% QoQ, which management attributed to better product mix and operating leverage. Electrolyte Salts was the standout segment, at INR131 million (up 1,378% YoY), while PTC fell 20% YoY and PASC fell 24% QoQ on dispatch delays after the new Dahej block was commissioned. Management maintained FY27 guidance of about 25% revenue growth and 20-22% EBITDA margin despite raw-material and freight cost inflation linked to the geopolitical conflict, which is being partly passed on to customers. The Jolva greenfield project is set to break ground within about 60 days, with commercial production targeted for early 2028.

financial_highlights.metric: EBITDA margin (Q4, as cited by analyst)
Pharma, Agro and Specialty Chemicals revenue

segments.name: Phase Transfer Catalysts (PTC)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR311 million, up 11% QoQ and down 20% YoY. Management describes steady organic growth in line with historical trends.

segments.name: Electrolyte Salts and Solutions (ESS)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR131 million, up 865% QoQ and 1,378% YoY. Management guides ESS to about 8-10% of FY27 revenue; hybrid battery commercial business expected from Q3 FY27.

segments.name: Pharma, Agro and Specialty Chemicals (PASC)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR358 million, up 10% YoY but down 24% QoQ, attributed to ramp-up delays at the new Dahej facility. Management expects about INR70-75 crore of new pharma revenue in FY27.

segments.name: Structured Directing Agents (SDA)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR525 million, up 52% YoY and down 2% QoQ. Management expects at least 20% growth in FY27 to INR250-300 crore, with the Euro 7 uptick seen from around July-August.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth of about 25%, with management saying it would stay conservative at 20-25% given geopolitical uncertainty.
FY27 EBITDA margin of 20-22%, unchanged despite raw-material inflation; management said 25% margin is achievable once the Dahej plant is fully operational.
ESS to contribute about 8-10% of FY27 revenue; hybrid battery business to begin commercial supply around Nov-Dec 2026.
SDA revenue to grow at least 20% to INR250-300 crore in FY27.
Pharma new add-on of INR70-75 crore in FY27; first product commercialised in Q1 and two more from Q3, on a campaign basis.
Current Dahej facility can reach INR850-900 crore revenue potential after minor bottleneck capex of INR10-12 crore a year, with full potential expected in FY28.
Jolva Phase 1 revenue potential INR400-500 crore; commercial production expected January-March 2028; capex about INR100 crore in FY27 and INR175 crore in FY28; total about INR250-270 crore.
Effective tax rate expected to decline as book and tax depreciation converge and the 10AA tax holiday benefit applies; cash tax paid in the quarter was about INR7 crore.
capex_capacity: New Dahej production block is fully operational on a commercial scale; trial production began in January 2026 and commercialisation in February 2026.
Current facility peak utilisation is about 80-85%; revenue potential from the current capacity is INR850-900 crore after debottlenecking.

Jolva greenfield project: groundbreaking expected in roughly 60 days (about July 2026) after civil construction bids; 18-20 months to commercial production; multi-phase build with a dedicated plant for a large agro product using an in-house technology.
Capex of about INR100 crore in FY27 and INR175 crore in FY28, both relating to Jolva; about INR100 crore of capex was capitalised in the recent period, which raised deferred tax.
demand_pricing: SDA demand is growing steadily ahead of Euro 7 emission norms (2027, starting in Europe); the company says it has a share of about 15% in a duopoly with Sarchem and expects share gains on Euro 7 programmes.
Raw-material prices (amines and crude/ammonia-linked inputs) rose about 30-40%; most customers accepted pass-through on new orders, while open orders were honoured and some customers resisted.
Amine supply was disrupted for 2-3 weeks in March 2026, costing production days, but availability has since normalised.
Agro intermediate orders have visibility through calendar 2026 and into 2027; management said it saw no ag-chem volume concern at its products.
Semiconductor chemical: first plant-scale batch (purity 99.99%, impurities below 1 ppb) to be dispatched in Q1 FY27 through integrators; commercialisation expected around end-2028 or early 2029.

qa_highlights.question: What are FY27 revenue growth and EBITDA margin expectations, given geopolitical cost pressure?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated about 25% revenue growth and 20-22% EBITDA margin; cost increases are only partly absorbed by customers, but the guidance was not changed.

qa_highlights.question: Is Q4 ESS run-rate sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is sustainable at around the same level each quarter; on an annual basis, FY27 ESS revenue could be about 4x Q4, from one application, with the hybrid battery application adding from late 2026.

qa_highlights.question: Why did PASC decline QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Dispatch delays after the new Dahej plant started production; orders are visible through end-2026 and demand is stable, and both agro products are now producing consistently.

qa_highlights.question: How did the tax rate reach 38% in Q4 and how will it move?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited loss carryforwards that disallowed 10AA benefit this year and about INR100 crore of capitalised capex raising deferred tax; the full-year rate is about 26% and should fall as book and tax depreciation converge.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Jolva timeline and investment?
qa_highlights.answer: Ground-breaking expected around mid-July 2026 after a design change reduced reactor count; production in January-March 2028; investment roughly INR250-270 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why pay dividend when short-term borrowings are rising?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it retains about 90% of earnings and distributes about 10% of net profit as dividend, which it considers fair to shareholders.

risks_watch: Raw-material and freight inflation from the geopolitical conflict; some customers refuse pass-through, which may dent EBITDA margin.
Euro 7 SDA ramp expected from July-August 2026; timing is unconfirmed and the business is concentrated in a duopoly with few customers.
Jolva schedule depends on groundbreaking in July 2026 and a 18-20 month build; the design was re-engineered, adding schedule risk.
PASC ramp at Dahej and the first pharma product's commercial timing (Q1 FY27) must be confirmed.
Rising short-term borrowings alongside dividend payout; interest cost and working capital are open questions.
Semiconductor commercialisation is still in validation and is not expected before late 2028 or early 2029.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand and the FY27 guidance, but cautious on macro risk; the CEO said he would stay conservative at 20-25% growth. Management was candid about PASC delays and the tax rate, and gave specific timelines and numbers, though some answers on Jolva and semiconductor timing were less precise.
key_quotes: The new block is now fully operational on commercial scale.
So, I would stay a little conservative with a prediction of 20% to 25%, give or take.

The Electrolyte Salts segment continued to scale gradually, supported by increasing consumption in energy storage applications.
